The game runs fine, the map works, and I had fun with most of the puzzles. It even had a decent amount of actual hidden object puzzles. Aside from some story faults, I will recommend it.

This is also one of the few hidden object games I've seen have a male protagonist, although that isn't saying much, because his only line of dialogue comes at the end of the bonus chapter and is not even voice acted. Still, though, and interesting novelty.

Speaking of the bonus story, that appeared to very quickly cobbled together, and the puzzles were just arbitrarily scattered, not clever. I didn't even realize I was playing the same character until I checked the in-game journal. Honestly, the Bonus story was completely unnecessary, rushed, and actively harmed the main story that you will have only just finished.

The main problem that annoyed me from the very start, however, was the fact that the game is set in the 1740's, and the narrator tells you that The Black Death has been over for about 50 years. This is in spite of the fact that THE Plague would have happened almost exactly 400 years before the story takes place. I realize there would still be incidents of bubonic plague up until the setting if the story, but they would not be spoken of with the same tone or language. This stupid error distracted me from the story the whole game, that and none of the women wearing anything close period-appropriate clothing. The main woman's clothing, in particular, is just AWFUL.
Loved the story and the game was nice, did not have any issues playing, everything was smooth. Loved the interview in the end of the main game, how interesting! The bonus story was a nice touch! :D

Vampire Legends The True Story of Kisilova is a well written, engaging and suspenseful hidden object adventure game where you get to meet interesting and lively characters. The townsfolk can be lovely, mysterious or downright spooky, and the hidden object sections are well drawn with plenty of objects to find. Some of the objects are very tiny and blend well into the background. But that's ok, as there's a hint button if you get stuck. 

The puzzles range from easy to solve to being challenging and needing creativity and thought. I liked the puzzle where you had to figure out the proper locations for each book on a bookshelf, by looking at the symbols on the bookshelf and the book spines. It's challenging, but not too hard, and feels rewarding once you figure it out. 

The puzzle where you had to figure out how to add the right amount of ingredients to make rakia was also interesting and challenging, and fun to solve. 

This game is very replayable and the puzzles and quests are well thought out. I found the lemon juice puzzle (where you had to find lemon juice and salt to remove rust) in the bonus story really enjoyable for some reason. Possibly because it was quite clever and the sound effects were very soothing. 

The soundtrack is excellent, with a moody atmosphere that matches the grim events in the story. You can also listen to different musical pieces in the game in the bonus features once you've finished playing the game, which I liked. 

The main game has one ending (which was enjoyable), and the bonus game has 2 endings which you can choose from. I liked both endings for the bonus game because they're both so different, and feel suspenseful and impactful. Both endings make you feel like your choices matter. 

I also enjoyed the game's bonus features where you can watch two short informative documentaries about the history of vampire myths in Serbia and the lovely photos of the village portrayed. The bonus features are available once you finish playing the game.

I'll start by saying that I usually love Artifex Mundi games, and that I was really looking forward to this game. Credit where credit is due, the artstyle is nice and there are plenty of scenes to investigate. All in all, it is not a bad game. The reason I leave a bad review is because of the frustration. 

Now I finished the game and the bonus game, so again, this was not unbearable. But there were a few things that bothered me. 
First was how illogical the items you needed to use/couldn't use sometimes were. For example, I couldn't break glass with a shovel but I could with a crowbar. It's just one example, but I had too many moments like this to proper enjoy the game. 
Second was the mix of old and modern items. The game is set in the 1700s, and overall it does a fairly good job of setting the scenes and items in that theme. A few times though, especially in the bonus chapter, it put in some modern items that broke the immersion a bit. 
Third probably has to due with the age of the game, but sometimes the colors look too much alike or the scenes are too pixellated to see the items you need. 

Overall, the game is not bad, just too frustrating for me to leave a good review.

Waited and played this for Halloween, although I only just got around to finishing it now. This you can tell from the art style and the simplicity of it that this is an older game, though this is not necessarily a bad thing.

There are no collectibles, no combining items in your inventory that I remember, and not a lot of other challenges in the game's achievements. I like having things to aim for when I play, but I also enjoy more straight forward entries like this one.

The setting and game are supposedly based on a real life event, although it's not clear how closely this follows the original events. (Obviously it can't be too close to reality since vampires are not real.) There are some pictures of Kisilova you can see in the extras for the game which are great, and I really enjoyed the bonus material they did include in the game, it's unique to find a game like this where the extras are things like photos of a real town.

Overall, I enjoyed it. The story was basic but easy to follow, there were a few interesting puzzles, a good amount of hidden object scenes, and a good amount of scenes and characters. There is also a bonus adventure that includes some locations not used in the main part of the game, and I always like it when bonus adventures include new areas instead of only retreading existing ones.

I will also say that some of the animations in the game are really impressive. Not everything is fully animated, but some of the animations of characters moving area more fluid and detailed than some hidden object games I play that were made in more recent years-- if they include any animation at all, a lot of games usually try to forgo them except for in specific cutscenes, which is OK too.

As for what I didn't like, some of the uses of some of the objects you collect were not exactly intuitive to me, and I got stuck a few times because I had an object to use, but the situation to use it in didn't initially make sense to me. I never got so stuck that I had to look up a guide though. The only other thing that bothered me, and this is endemic of a lot of older hidden object games or ones that take place in an earlier time in history, is that I had to look up some of the names of some of the hidden objects in the hidden object puzzles. This obviously isn't helpful for finishing a puzzle in under a minute for the achievement, but I was able to get that done without needing to replay it and try again. For example, no idea what a spud bar is. (Although I do now! Sometimes these games can be a neat vocab lesson.)

In summary, this is a nice no-frills adventure that provides a simpler experience if you want a break from collectible hunting and difficulty achievements, or if you just don't enjoy those things to begin with.

The hidden object puzzles should have been a little more straightforward and the other aspects of the game should have had a little more meat on the bone for players who are experienced with other AM titles. I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

[quote][b]S U M M A R Y[/b][/quote]

[u][b]Vampire Legends: The True Story of Kisilova[/b][/u] is a casual point-and-click puzzle game whose story is based on real-life events. Overall, I recommend the game but only when it goes on sale because there is only 3-4 hours of gameplay; however, it provides a great casual experience thanks to its relatively simple puzzles, its story which is based on historical events that it follows quite faithfully, and its overall production value which is surprisingly higher than you might initially assume.

[hr][/hr]
[quote][b]A C H I E V E M E N T S[/b][/quote]

The game has 10 easy achievements which can take between 2-4 hours to get depending on whether you're speedrunning the game with the help of a guide or just casually enjoying it.

[hr][/hr]
[quote][b]R E V I E W[/b][/quote]

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
The gameplay is standard for the genre: you gather objects which you have to combine with other objects, or use in certain spots, in order to acquire key items and advance the story. I've played a few games in this genre so far and haven't enjoyed most of them because you collect far too many objects too quickly, which makes figuring out what to use where feel like a tedious chore, and because they expect you to combine seemingly esoteric objects together but provide few to no hints linking them together.

Thankfully, this is not the case here as you are rarely over-burdened with too many objects, it's obvious what each object does and where it must be used, there are a generous amount of clues on the standard difficulty, and there are in-game hints if you get stuck. Additionally, the game has a map which has helpful notes reminding you of things that you have yet to interact with in each area as well as a fast-travel feature to do away with the monotony of traversing through the same areas over and over again. The gameplay also has some added diversity due to the inclusion of hidden object scenes, which I found surprisingly fun and challenging, and various mini-games. Altogether, the simpler puzzles give the game a more casual experience which allows you to enjoy the rest of the game to its fullest.

However, you unlock a bonus chapter after completing the game and this chapter is more akin to the games that I didn't enjoy because it does inundate you with a large number of seemingly obscure objects very quickly. It still wasn't that difficult but I found it to be somewhat overbearing and didn't enjoy it nearly as much as the main story. This bonus chapter also has almost no dialogue and very few story sequences in total which detracted from the overall experience and makes it feel more like a puzzle rush instead of a full-fledged game.

[h3]Graphics[/h3]
The graphics are surprisingly good with very nicely-drawn backgrounds which are pleasing to look at and detailed character art which is actually animated during some cutscenes. The animation ranges in quality from decent to pretty crude and unnatural-looking, but some cutscenes aren't animated when they should be and you end up watching still images move across the background which is quite jarring but isn't a huge deal. Maybe their budget was running out at that point.

[h3]Sound[/h3]
The music is purely atmospheric in nature and you probably won't even notice it while playing the game. That being said, it does fit the game nicely but it isn't anything special by any means.

The game has voice acting, which was pleasantly surprising, and it's unexpectedly good for the most part. Some characters sound out-of-place for the time and setting of the game while some individual lines sound exaggerated and over-the-top. Despite this, it still added to the experience and enhanced the somewhat generic story.

[h3]Story[/h3]
The story is based on real-life events, and has been adapted to a very clichéd [u][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whodunit]whodunit[/url][/u] murdery mystery, but I still found myself quite engrossed by it; however, it is extremely linear, has a few typos, and has a few ridiculous plot devices which you'll have to suspend your disbelief for (one example being you needing a key for a gate when you could easily climb it or go around).

[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]
The game also comes with a number of neat extras that add to the overall package: a picture gallery of real-life Kisiljevo, concept art for various characters and backgrounds, a music player, two interviews with people from the development team, and even a neat UI showcasing the developer's vast library of games.

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
Overall, I recommend the game — it's surprisingly good and the time flew by while I was playing. That being said, its regular price feels a little steep for the amount of playtime you'll get out of it so I suggest waiting for it to go on sale which it regularly does for [u][url=https://steamdb.info/app/414660/]90% off at 1.00 USD[/url][/u].

Vampire Legends: The True Story of Kisilova é um jogo de aventura com elementos de terror, baseado no primeiro caso documentado de vampirismo!

Europa do século XVIII: cinquenta anos depois de uma grande praga ter varrido a terra da dinastia dos Habsburgos, os súditos do imperador estão novamente em perigo. Uma série de mortes horríveis e inexplicáveis ocorrem na remota cidade sérvia de Kisilova. Temendo que a praga possa estar atacando novamente, os moradores começam a fugir de suas casas. Convocados pelo próprio Príncipe de Württemberg, emissários imperiais vêm a Kisilova para investigar os eventos e evitar novas mortes.

A heroína e seu companheiro têm que liderar uma investigação, questionar as testemunhas, explorar todos os cantos e recantos da cidade e resolver muitos quebra-cabeças. Eles serão capazes de descobrir os segredos dos dignitários locais e descobrir a identidade do estranho encapuzado que tenta frustrar seus planos?

O destino de Kisilova e do Império está em suas mãos!

Believe it or not, but this game actually IS based on true events. In 1725, Imperial Provisor Ernst Frombald was asked to investigate alleged vampire activity in Kisilova, Serbia, by rummaging through sheds, cabinets and drawers of every single occupant of the town, reading their private diaries, breaking their home decorations, sorting books in bookshelves, wine bottles in cellars, and even skulls in local crypt. Frombald documented this and it has become one of the most famous vampire cases in history.

Jokes aside, I love these kinds of games with their corny graphics and easy-to-medium difficulty puzzles. Recommended :)

Знаете, перед игрой не терпелось посмотреть видосы-интервью жителей деревни, это было действительно хорошим опытом, окунулся в особую атмосферу. К сожалению игровой опыт выпил все соки из это же атмосферы.

Из плюсов хочу отметить, что сюжет вносится повествованием как самих героев, так и записками, письмами и книгами (которые Я решил пропустить,), не шарю в части сюжета, но для меня он оказался на таком уровне, что лицо от фейспалмов не пострадало.

Однако, босс файт, если это можно так называть, не был проработан.

В первую очередь к минусам хотелось бы отнести, завышенные ожидания из-за положительных отзывов. Обычно фанаты игр на поиск предметов, несмотря на сниженные требования к играм, которые были разработаны не самими АМ, расписывают всё осторожно и по фактам.

Среди нас много визуалов. Но тут отрисованы только герои, а всё остальное какое-то блеклое, не сочное, не естественное. Картинка не очень в основном сюжете, хотя в бонусе показалось  получше, возможно за счёт того, что там иной сеттинг, и графика к нему подошла лучше.

Насчёт музыки: вот что-то не то и не так, чего-то не хватило. Не хватило и погружения в этот мир. Поверил только в локацию с лягушками на берегу реки.
